title: Ἁλιεὺς καὶ σμαρίς
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 26. Text as printed, including Chambry's editorial punctuation (« », ⟨ ⟩ for editorial supplements). Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Ἁλιεὺς τὸ δίκτυον χαλάσας ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ ἀνήνεγκε σμαρίδα.
sentences.tr: Halieus to diktyon chalasas en tēi thalassēi anēnenke smarida.
sentences.l: A fisherman, having let his net down into the sea, brought up a sprat.
sentences.n: χαλάω is to slacken, and so to let down. σμαρίς is a small Mediterranean fish, probably the picarel; “sprat” stands in for it here, since all that matters is that it is too small to be worth keeping. It is a feminine noun, so the fish is spoken of, and speaks, as “she.”

sentences.t: Σμικρὰ δὲ οὖσα ἱκέτευεν αὐτὸν νῦν μὲν μὴ λαβεῖν αὐτήν, ἀλλ’ ἐᾶσαι, διὰ τὸ σμικρὰν τυγχάνειν.
sentences.tr: Smikra de ousa hiketeuen auton nyn men mē labein autēn, all’ easai, dia to smikran tynchanein.
sentences.l: And being small she besought him not to take her now, but to let her be, on account of happening to be small.
sentences.n: διὰ τὸ … τυγχάνειν is an articular infinitive: the article τό turns the infinitive into a noun that διά can govern, “on account of happening to be small.” τυγχάνω with a bare predicate adjective (σμικράν) means “to be, as it happens,” the participle ὤν being left out.

sentences.t: « Ἀλλ’ ὅταν αὐξυνθῶ καὶ μεγάλη, φησί, γένωμαι, συλλαβεῖν με δυνήσῃ, ἐπεὶ καὶ εἰς μείζονά σοι ὠφέλειαν ἔσομαι. »
sentences.tr: « All’ hotan auxynthō kai megalē, phēsi, genōmai, syllabein me dynēsēi, epei kai eis meizona soi ōpheleian esomai. »
sentences.l: « But whenever I have grown and become large, » says she, « you will be able to catch me, since I shall also be for a greater benefit to you. »
sentences.i: « But when I have grown big, » she said, « you will be able to catch me — and I shall be of far more use to you then. »
sentences.n: φησί, “says she,” is dropped into the middle of her own sentence: Greek puts the verb of speaking in parenthetically, and the present tense is a historic present in a past narrative. ὅταν with the aorist subjunctive (αὐξυνθῶ, γένωμαι) is the general future case, “when once I have…”. εἰς … ὠφέλειαν ἔσομαι, “I shall be for a benefit,” is a periphrasis for “I shall serve as a benefit.” αὐξύνομαι is a late by-form of αὐξάνομαι, “grow.”

sentences.t: Καὶ ὁ ἁλιεὺς εἶπεν· « Ἀλλ’ ἔγωγε ἄνους ἂν εἴην, εἰ τὸ ἐν χερσὶ παρεὶς κέρδος, κἂν σμικρὸν ᾖ, τὸ προσδοκώμενον, κἂν μέγα ὑπάρχῃ, ἐλπίζοιμι. »
sentences.tr: Kai ho halieus eipen· « All’ egōge anous an eiēn, ei to en chersi pareis kerdos, kan smikron ēi, to prosdokōmenon, kan mega hyparchēi, elpizoimi. »
sentences.l: And the fisherman said: « Well, I for my part would be witless if, having let go the gain in my hands, even if it be small, I should hope for the one expected, even if it be great. »
sentences.i: And the fisherman said: « Then I should be a fool, if I let slip the gain in my hands, small though it be, and set my hopes on one merely expected, however great. »
sentences.n: A future-less-vivid condition: optative in both limbs, εἰ … ἐλπίζοιμι and ἂν εἴην, “if I should hope … I would be.” κἄν is καὶ ἐάν crushed together, “even if,” with the subjunctive. ἄνους is ἀ- with νοῦς, “without wits.” The whole sentence is a formula the collection reuses: at fable 8 the hawk answers in the same frame, Ἀλλ’ ἔγωγε ἀπόπληκτος ἂν εἴην, εἰ τὴν ἐν χερσὶν … παρεὶς …, with βορά, food, where this fisherman has κέρδος, gain.

sentences.t: Ὁ μῦθος δηλοῖ ὅτι ἀλόγιστος ἂν εἴη ὁ δι’ ἐλπίδα μείζονος τὰ ἐν χερσὶν ἀφεὶς σμικρὰ ὄντα.
sentences.tr: Ho mythos dēloi hoti alogistos an eiē ho di’ elpida meizonos ta en chersin apheis smikra onta.
sentences.l: The fable shows that senseless would be the man who, through hope of something greater, has let go the things in his hands because they are small.
sentences.i: The fable shows that a man would be senseless who, in hope of something greater, lets slip what is in his hands because it is small.
sentences.n: Almost the same moral as fable 8's, in almost the same words (ἀλόγιστοι … δι’ ἐλπίδα μειζόνων τὰ ἐν χερσίν): the collection keeps fixed phrases for its recurring lessons. ὁ … ἀφείς is an articular participle standing as a noun, “the one who has let go.” σμικρὰ ὄντα is causal, “because they are small.” ἂν εἴη is the potential optative again.
